name: Jira issue to Bitbucket PR
description: Watch a Jira Cloud project for issues with a configurable label and automatically open a Bitbucket pull request for each new issue found. The target Bitbucket repo is read from the ticket body - no repo parameter required at deploy time.

atlassian-rovo.message: Reads implementation-ready issues and posts progress back to Jira.

bitbucket.message: Clones the target repository, pushes a branch, and opens the pull request.

exampleImplementation:
Trigger: cron polling (e.g. every 5 minutes)
Required integrations: Atlassian Rovo MCP for Jira access and a Bitbucket connection. On OpenHands Cloud and Enterprise the poller reads and comments on Jira through the connected Atlassian Rovo MCP server, so it needs no Jira API token; the conversation it starts pushes with the connected Bitbucket integration, or commits through the Bitbucket tools of the same Atlassian Rovo MCP server when it has no token. A local Agent Canvas needs a Jira API token and a Bitbucket token as secrets instead.

1. Connect Atlassian Rovo MCP and Bitbucket, then collect the Jira site, label to watch, and cron schedule from the user, and set git_provider to bitbucket. A local Agent Canvas also needs the Jira base URL, email, and API token secret name. No Bitbucket repo is needed at deploy time - each ticket must include the target repo (workspace/repo on bitbucket.org) in its body.
2. Search the Jira Cloud instance for open issues carrying the configured label.
3. Deduplicate against a KV-store-backed set of already-processed issue keys so re-runs never create duplicate PRs.
4. For each new issue, start an independent OpenHands agent conversation that extracts the Bitbucket repo from the ticket body, clones it, creates a branch named after the Jira key, implements or scaffolds the requested change, and opens a pull request.
5. Immediately after the conversation is created, post a Jira comment on the issue: 'I'm on it: <conversation URL>'.
6. Persist the processed issue key immediately after dispatching so the next poll skips it.
